verify_before_render: GitHub API 2026-10-16: 867 stars, 27 forks, created 2026-10-13, Apache-2.0. Install npm i @outcrawl/scout, Node 22+.
Needs an Outcrawl key (README: free 1,000 credits/month) plus any chat-completions model key or a local model endpoint.
Catches spoken: smoothest on Outcrawl's cloud; two keys; sites may block bots. Visuals are our own cards; no copied demo GIF.

scenes.heading: IT *BROWSES* FOR YOU
scenes.say: Tell this agent the task, and it opens a real browser and does it.

scenes.heading: MEET *SCOUT*
scenes.say: It is Scout, an open-source browser agent from Outcrawl.

scenes.heading: HOW IT *WORKS*
scenes.say: It reads the page, clicks, types and scrolls until the job is done, then reports back.

scenes.heading: DEVS *NOTICED*
scenes.label: GitHub · first three days
scenes.say: It picked up over eight hundred GitHub stars in its first three days.

scenes.heading: ONE *NPM INSTALL*
scenes.say: Install it with npm. You bring an Outcrawl key, and a key for whichever model you like.

scenes.heading: BEFORE YOU *RUN IT*
scenes.say: The catches: the smoothest ride is on Outcrawl's own cloud, you need two keys to start, and some sites will still block a bot. But it is Apache two, and it can run on your own machine.
What would you send a browser agent to do? Comment SCOUT and I will pin the repo.

Scout by Outcrawl is an open-source (Apache-2.0) browser agent: describe a task in plain words and it reads, clicks, types and scrolls in a real browser until the job is done. 867 GitHub stars in three days. Source: https://github.com/outcrawlai/scout
